_comment: THE INCLUDE LIST for the paint page, and the source of truth for what it
loads. The page fetches exactly this -- no candidate list, no directory
scan -- so adding a provider to the browser runtime is an edit here and
nothing else. Load order is the order these appear in.
RenderProvider before PaintProvider because a PaintSurface takes a Surface,
and ShellProvider last so the navigator comes up in the embedded terminal.
NAMES, NOT PATHS. These are fetched from the SHARED artifact directory --
/wasm/, which is bin/wasm/ mounted by the serve scripts -- and staged into
MEMFS under the bare name, because preload_web_modules dlopens by name and
run_script opens by name. The url and the staged name are different things.
Optional "base": pin that directory (a CDN, a second origin) and the page
skips its own same-origin-then-beside-then-remote walk. See resolveWasmBase
in index.html. "glue" comes from the same base -- it and etcs.wasm are one
link's output, and a mismatched pair fails before any ETCS code runs.
_scripts: Staged into the browser's filesystem by the page, under these names, before
main() runs -- so each one must also answer over HTTP. They are mounted from
ONE list, ../paint_mounts.etcs, which every server runs (serve_paint.etcs at
its root, ETCS's run_website.etcs and run_tls_website.etcs under /paint/).
Adding a script here means adding its mount line there -- a name the page
asks for and no server mounts is a 404, and render_frames.etcs is the frame
pump, so losing it leaves a black canvas on a working runtime.
A NAME MAY BE A PATH: the page creates the directories first
(FS.mkdirTree), which is what lets a script be staged at the same relative
path the OS side reads it from, so boot_paint_panels.etcs's `detach` and
`run` lines are spelled once for both substrates rather than twice.
_glue: The emscripten loader output, STAGED AS .js: served extensionless it arrives
as application/octet-stream, which the browser warns is not a valid
